description: Input and output devices, often referred to as peripheral devices, are hardware components used to send data to a computer and receive processed information from it. This topic is highly crucial for the Computer Knowledge section of various competitive exams.

sections.title: Major Input Devices
sections.description: Hardware devices that allow users to enter data, commands, and programs into the CPU for processing.

key_concepts.explanation: The most common text-based input device. It consists of alphanumeric keys, function keys (F1 to F12), modifier keys (Ctrl, Alt, Shift), and navigation keys. The standard layout is QWERTY.
A pointing device invented by Douglas Engelbart. It is used to control the cursor in a Graphical User Interface (GUI) and perform actions like click, double-click, and drag-and-drop.
A pointing device consisting of a stick that pivots on a base. It is primarily used for playing video games, operating flight simulators, and controlling CAD (Computer-Aided Design) systems.
An input device that optically reads physical documents, photographs, or graphics and converts them into digital images for computer processing.

sections.title: Optical Recognition Devices
sections.description: Specialized input devices that read marks, characters, or barcodes on paper and convert them directly into digital data.

key_associations.extra_info: Used extensively in competitive exams to read and evaluate pen or pencil marks on specially printed OMR answer sheets.
Technology used to convert scanned images of printed or handwritten text into machine-encoded, editable digital text.
Used by banks to quickly process and clear cheques. It reads characters printed with a special magnetic ink containing iron oxide.
An optical scanner that reads printed barcodes (patterns of light and dark lines) to instantly fetch product pricing and inventory details.

sections.title: Major Output Devices
sections.description: Hardware components that display, print, or project the processed data (results) into a human-readable format.

key_concepts.explanation: Also known as VDU (Visual Display Unit). It provides 'soft copy' visual output. Major display technologies include CRT (Cathode Ray Tube), LCD (Liquid Crystal Display), and LED (Light Emitting Diode).
An external hardware output device that takes electronic data stored on a computer and generates a 'hard copy' of it on physical paper.
A specialized output device used to produce high-quality, large-scale vector graphics, architectural blueprints, and engineering drawings using automated pens.

sections.title: Types of Printers
sections.description: Printers are broadly classified into two main categories based on their printing mechanism: Impact and Non-Impact printers.

key_concepts.explanation: These printers form characters by physically striking a ribbon against the paper (similar to a typewriter). They are noisy and slower. Examples: Dot Matrix Printer, Daisy Wheel Printer, and Line Printer.

These printers form characters and images without any direct physical contact between the print head and the paper. They are fast, silent, and produce high-quality output. Examples: Laser Printer, Inkjet Printer, and Thermal Printer.

key_associations.extra_info: Uses a laser beam and static electricity to attract dry ink powder (toner) onto the paper. It is the fastest printer offering the highest text quality.
Creates digital images by propelling microscopic droplets of liquid ink onto the paper. Highly suitable for color photo printing.

sections.title: I/O Mixed Devices and Important Facts
sections.description: Devices that function as both Input and Output simultaneously, along with highly tested factual data.

key_associations.extra_info: Acts as an input device by registering touch gestures and an output device by displaying the visual interface.
Converts digital signals from a computer to analog signals for telephone lines (Output), and vice versa (Input).
Combines a microphone (for audio input) and speakers (for audio output) into a single wearable unit.

important_facts.fact: The modern QWERTY keyboard layout was invented by Christopher Latham Sholes in 1868.
The resolution of a monitor is measured in Pixels (Picture Elements). A higher number of pixels results in a sharper and clearer image.
The speed of a printer is measured in PPM (Pages Per Minute), while its printing quality/resolution is measured in DPI (Dots Per Inch).
